about: Four photographs taken round Canada Water Library, SE16, and given to the project under CC0 by the owner. This file holds the hand-made part: what each photo shows, how each building was identified, and the facade regions to rectify. The measurements are made by the logged operation rectify-facade-patches and the graph by lift-contrib-photos (magpie/cwplans/tools/contrib-photos.mjs). Skills: docklands-data-curation ('Contributed photos'), photo-view-reconstruction.
creator: danbri (project owner)
time: about 16:30 BST (owner); the files carry no EXIF time, GPS or camera data
sun: 2026-10-06 15:30 UTC: azimuth 238.7 deg true, altitude 16.3 deg (astronomy-engine, tools/view-mcp sunAt)
osm_extract: openstreetmap.fr greater_london-latest.osm.pbf (data as of 2026-10-01, fetched 2026-10-02; data-register osm_extracts osmfr-greater-london; magpie/cwplans/data/raw/docklands/), cut with osmium to -0.062,51.491,-0.036,51.505
model: magpie/cwplans/docklands/data/area.js built 2026-10-03; model index, height above the ground (height_m), ground (base_m_od), roof (top_m_od) and height source at that build. Correction 2026-10-06: the first version of this file gave the height above the ground as top_m_od, and 76.5 m (82.2 - 5.7) as Ontario Point's height.

ontario-point.name: Ontario Point

model.height_source: lidar (90th percentile of DSM minus DTM, so the roof frame is in it)

ontario-point.footprint: near-square, sides 24.2 m (bearing 27 deg) and 24.0 m (bearing 149 deg), from the OSM outline

faces_seen.south-west: main face in photo 1 (normal 239 deg: it faced the sun)
faces_seen.north-west: narrow face on the left in photo 1

facade.south_west_face: Symmetric, 24.0 m wide: corner pier | 3-pane bay | pier | pane | louvre | pane | pier | pane | louvre | pane | pier | pane | louvre | pane | pier | 3-pane bay | corner pier. 12 glazing panes, 3 dark vertical louvre strips (full height), 4 inner piers, 2 corner piers. Panes about 1.2 m, louvre pitch about 4.6 m (rectified patch ontario-point-sw-top, face width from OSM).
facade.vertical_module: A thick slab band every two floors and a thin transom halfway between: about 12 two-floor units above the ground floor. Floor about 3.1 m (LiDAR height 82.2 m above the ground, less a roof frame of about 4.5 m, over 25 levels).
facade.north_west_face: Glazed winter gardens (balconies closed by glass), one row a floor, on a dark frame.
facade.top: Open roof frame about one and a half floors tall: thin vertical fins on a top beam, over a glass balustrade (roof terrace). A tall thin fin rises at the west corner.
facade.base: Double-height ground floor, the name ONTARIO POINT in metal letters at the left of the south-west face.
facade.materials: Light warm-grey stone or precast piers and spandrels; blue-reflective glass; dark grey louvre strips.
facade.how: judged from photo 1 and the rectified patches; counts checked on the full-width patch

identified_by: the name ONTARIO POIN(T) on the building in photo 1
OSM way 204580680 has addr:housename Ontario Point and 25 levels
floor count: about 12 two-floor units plus the ground floor, about 25 levels; LiDAR height 82.2 m above the ground (with the roof frame)

canada-water-library.name: Canada Water Library
canada-water-library.footprint: longest sides 42.0 m (bearing 73 deg) and 34.8 m (bearing 110 deg), from the OSM outline; the building widens upward (an inverted pyramid), so the footprint is smaller than the roof

facade.wall: Expanded-metal panels with a diamond mesh, warm grey-brown (bronze), in a staggered panel grid. The walls lean out: the building is wider at the top.
facade.windows: Tall framed windows that project from the wall as boxes, 2 panes across and 3 to 4 high, bronze frames; five on the north face in photo 2, at differing heights.
facade.base: Glazed ground floor with a black fascia and the words CANADA WATER LIBRARY in white capitals; a maroon double door with a leisure centre advertisement.
facade.how: judged from photo 2 and the rectified patch library-north-wall

identified_by: the words CANADA WATER LIBRARY on the building

tiles.what: the south-west face of Ontario Point (CC0 photo, sunlit)
tiles.how: Left half of the south-west face, from the outer edge of the corner pier to the middle of the middle louvre strip (348 of about 696 px), and its mirror image for the right half (the face is symmetric). Four two-floor units, from the middle of one thick band to the fourth band below (95 px each). Width = the OSM face, 24.0 m; height = 8 floors x 3.1 m. The metric aspect from the vanishing points (1.66 to 1.73) gives 22.3 m, 10% less. Every wall of the model gets this tile, so the north-west face (glazed winter gardens) shows the south-west pattern.

tiles.what: the dark part of The Founding (CC0 photo, in shade)
tiles.how: Two bays (pier middle to pier middle, 144 px each) by four floors (slab middle to slab middle, 82 px each) of the dark charcoal part. Height = 4 x 3.0 m (the model's own 3 m a level for this tower); width from the metric aspect of the photo (1.59 to 1.65): 6.5 m. The red-framed part with balconies is not in the tile: the model has one outline for the whole tower.

tiles.what: the bronze expanded-metal mesh of Canada Water Library (CC0 photo, in shade)
tiles.how: Mesh only, from between and above the window boxes: the window boxes are not in a regular grid, so a repeating tile would add windows the building does not have. Scale judged: a window box (2 panes, 125 px) is about 2.2 m; aspect 0.91 from the vanishing points.

tiles.what: a vector pattern of Columbia Point and Regina Point (from a CC0 photo; colours judged)
tiles.how: Drawn from the rectified face of Columbia Point (photo 3, against the sun): one floor (3.09 m = 61.7 m / 20 levels) by one bay of 4.8 m: red-brown panel 1.2 m, window 1.2 m, cream pier 1.1 m, window 1.2 m, over a cream band at the slab. Widths from the photo with its metric aspect (1.35 to 1.44 from the vanishing points). The colours are judged material colours, not measured: the photo is against the sun. Left out: the recessed balcony row every fourth floor (one bay) and the glazed stair column. Regina Point is its twin and gets the same tile.
